question: What will the USDA Choice boxed beef cutout value (600–900 lb) be on September 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is $376.17 (Sep 4, last print before Labor Day), with five sessions flat in a $375.8-$379.8 band. Reference class (post-Labor-Day mid-September Choice cutout, 2019-2025) implies a median ~1.4% two-week seasonal decline, i.e. ~$371 -- September is reliably the transition into the Sept/Oct seasonal low as grilling demand ends and holiday rib buying has not yet begun. I adjust the median up to $374 because the bearish forces are already partly priced (the market fell $12 off the Aug 25 peak and then stabilized) while the supportive forces are unusually strong: packer margins of -$200 to -$300/head, slaughter down ~25k head year-over-year, Tyson closing/selling three plants, and fed supplies tight through year end -- the same configuration that produced the $363 to $388 rebound in August. Bearish news (larger beef imports, Mexican cattle resuming via an Arizona port) mainly hits live cattle and lean trimmings rather than the domestic Choice cutout on a two-week horizon. Dispersion is wide and slightly left-skewed: this series trends rather than random-walks, and the sharp post-Labor-Day break (2021: -$54 in a month) is the fatter tail. No human prediction market prices this contract, so no crowd blend.

calls.reconciliation: Seven disputes listed and classified below. Settled FACTUALLY: (a) the '+6.5% YoY slaughter' claim in Runs 2 and 3 is a holiday-alignment artifact -- Labor Day 2025 fell Sep 1 so the year-ago comparison week had four kill days against 2026's full five; Run 1's day-matched Friday figure (97k vs 103k) and Run 2's own 'production -3.1% vs same week last year, -7.9% YTD' both invert the sign, so supply is running below year-ago and that bearish input is removed. (b) Publication risk is nil: Sep 17 2026 is an ordinary Thursday and the fiscal year runs to Sep 30, so the shutdown fallback cannot engage. (c) The August series conflict is settled AGAINST Runs 2/3: their Aug 17-19 trio (379.57/391.15/394.99) is the same trio Run 1 traced to IndexBox with inconsistent dating, and it contradicts the question background's own description of August (low 360s to nearly 389, mid-August ~363); all sources agree on Aug 21/25/28 and on every September print, so I use peak ~388.5 and treat the market as -3.2% off its high, not -4.8%, which trims the 'already realized' credit. NOT SETTLED: packer margin sign, -$200/-$300 per head (Runs 1, 2, contemporaneous roundups) versus +$200 (Run 3, a quarterly lender outlook) -- no web access this run, the two may describe different periods, and since the sign flips the slaughter response it stays as uncertainty in the dispersion rather than a median shift. JUDGMENT calls I took: live cattle at a 14-month low is second-order for an 8-session cutout forecast because the cutout is the numerator of packer margin, not a follower of cattle price (contra Runs 2, 3); and the wide Choice/Select spread is bearish for Choice, not bullish -- all three runs read it as evidence of tight Choice supply, but the spread's summer width is a grilling-season middle-meat artifact that compresses into fall, and Sep 4's Select +5.15 against Choice -0.73 is that compression starting. That is my one real departure from the pool, and it roughly cancels the upward push from settling the slaughter artifact, which is why the median lands at 372 rather than the runs' 372-374 by a different route. Reference class carried forward from all three runs (post-Labor-Day to mid-September, conditioned on an August peak); dispersion carried near Run 3's because both rival August series independently imply a ~$20-25 eight-day move occurred last month. No human market prices this contract -- Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold and bookmakers checked independently by all three runs, none found, CME's Boxed Beef Index is non-tradeable -- so there is no crowd anchor and no blend.
